page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 1 physical core with 2 threads per core and a 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. Storage is network-attached with a local capacity of 1 GB, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no onboard GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with read-only operations categorized as weak, though large block write bandwidth achieves average tier performance. Text processing is a relative strength, scoring in the top 25% on Geekbench.

Given its hardware profile, this server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, and simple text processing tasks. It is less optimal for database operations, which scored in the bottom 10% on Passmark, or multi-threaded compilation and heavy parallel processing. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance for its single-threaded strengths, making it a cost-efficient option for entry-level general-purpose hosting, lightweight APIs, or development environments that do not require high memory bandwidth or local storage.
